bull_bear.body:
- Mini Ratna (Cat-I) status and schedule 'B' CPSE standing under the administrative control of the Ministry of Coal
- 85% subsidiary of Coal India Limited, giving a captive in-house consultancy relationship with CIL and its subsidiaries
- Described as a leading mining consultancy organization; over the last seven financial years CMPDIL has captured the largest share of jobs in both quantity and value
- Nationwide delivery network of seven Regional Institutes plus Ranchi headquarters
- Full-spectrum service stack under one roof spanning exploration, planning & design, engineering, laboratories, environment, IT and specialised services
- Nodal agency role for all S&T schemes funded by the Ministry of Coal and R&D schemes funded by the R&D Board of CIL
- In-house CPCB approved environmental laboratories supporting the environmental services line
- Strategic entry into critical minerals via the REE Exploration License for the Navatala-Deogarh Block (Rajasthan) and transaction advisory that enabled CIL to obtain the Ontillu REE License
- Strategic partnerships through MoUs with RITES Limited and Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL), with an MoU including NTPC Mining Limited (NML) under finalization
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Concentration on the Coal India Limited ecosystem — The Company's core role is in-house consultancy to CIL and its subsidiaries; the Board's Report frames FY 2025-26 progress explicitly as 'expanding its presence beyond the CIL ecosystem' and 'expanding its consultancy footprint beyond Coal India Limited', which implies the bulk of work continues to originate inside the parent group and that outside-CIL business (Rs 131.02 crore of orders in the year) is still a small complement.
- Dependence on the coal sector and coal-linked capital cycle — The listed service lines — geological exploration and drilling for in-situ coal reserves, project reports for underground and opencast mines, coalfield master plans, coal beneficiation, utilisation and handling plants — are almost entirely coal-driven, so demand tracks coal exploration and mine-development activity rather than a diversified end-market.
- Execution risk on the diversification strategy — Growth beyond CIL depends on winning work from Central and State Government organizations, PSUs and private enterprises, and on MoUs (RITES, BSNL, and an NTPC Mining Limited MoU still at various stages of finalization). These are stated as expected to enhance the service portfolio and business prospects, i.e. benefits are not yet contracted.
- Entry into new, unproven domains (critical minerals and REE) — The REE Exploration License for the Navatala-Deogarh Block (Rajasthan) and the advisory-enabled Ontillu REE License mark a 'strategic entry into the critical mineral exploration domain'; a new domain carries geological, technical and commercial uncertainty relative to the established coal consultancy franchise.
- Government / regulatory ownership and policy dependence — The Company operates as a Mini Ratna (Cat-I) government company whose services are substantially provided into government-directed programmes; the pace of exploration, project sanctioning and consultancy demand is therefore tied to government policy and budgetary decisions rather than to independent commercial demand.
- Pricing and competitive pressure in an open consultancy market — The Report stresses the need for continuous efforts to enhance market outreach, deliver customized technical solutions and maintain high standards of quality and professionalism to sustain its 'competitive edge' — an acknowledgement that outside-CIL work is contested and must be won on merit against other consultancies.
- People- and capability-intensive delivery model — The service portfolio (planning, design, engineering, laboratory analysis, geomatics, ventilation and gas surveys, NDT, mine support design) is delivered by specialised technical manpower and laboratories across seven Regional Institutes and the Ranchi headquarter; capability, retention and equipment currency are the binding constraints on capacity.
- Geographically dispersed delivery footprint — Operations span a Ranchi headquarter plus seven Regional Institutes at Asansol, Dhanbad, Ranchi, Nagpur, Bilaspur, Singrauli and Bhubaneswar, alongside client assignments in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and an international assignment in Mozambique, which adds coordination and delivery-oversight complexity.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Limited provides consultancy support in coal and mineral exploration, including geological, geophysical, hydrological and environmental data generation, to Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries as well as to outside companies. Its service lines span geological exploration & drilling, project planning & design, engineering services, R&D, laboratory services, environmental services, information technology, human resource development and specialised services such as geomatics/remote sensing, ventilation and gas surveys and non-destructive testing. It operates from a Headquarter at Gondwana Place, Kanke Road, Ranchi and seven Regional Institutes, serving Central and State Government organizations, PSUs and private sector enterprises alongside the CIL ecosystem.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Geological Exploration & Drilling:** Detailed geological exploration of regionally explored blocks, Multi-probe geophysical logging, High resolution shallow seismic survey, Hydro geological investigation, Identification of coal bed methane resources
- **Project Planning & Design:** Feasibility reports, Detailed project reports, Detailed engineering drawings for underground and opencast mines, Master plans of coalfields, Coal and mineral beneficiation and utilisation plant design, Coal handling plant design, Techno-economic evaluation for investment decisions
- **Engineering Services:** Detailed design of systems and sub-systems for mines, Beneficiation and utilisation plants, Coal handling plants, Power supply systems and workshops, Architectural planning & design
- **Research & Development:** Nodal agency for S&T schemes funded by Ministry of Coal, R&D schemes funded by R&D Board of CIL, Applied research in mining, beneficiation, utilisation, environment and exploration
- **Laboratory Services:** Analysis of mine gases, air, water and noise, Coal core sample and washability characteristics testing, Physico-mechanical strength of strata, Petrography studies, Non-Destructive Testing (NDT)
- **Environmental Services:** Environment Management Plan preparation, implementation and monitoring, Air, water and noise analysis at in-house CPCB approved laboratories, Mine closure plan preparation and monitoring, Slope stability study for OB and Highwall, Environmental carrying capacity and riverine ecosystem studies, Remote sensing satellite data based land use monitoring for entire CIL mines
- **Information Technology:** Information technology services
- **Human Resource Development:** Human resource development services
- **Specialised Services:** Geomatics including Remote Sensing, Ventilation & Gas survey in mines, Controlled Blasting, Performance evaluation of new explosives, Mining Electronics, Mine capacity Assessment, Mine Support Design, Rock Mass Rating (RMR), Non-Destructive Testing, Management System Consultancy, Measurement of Coal and OBR
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Coal India Limited (CIL) — related party: Holding company; CMPDIL is an 85% subsidiary of CIL. CMPDIL renders in-house consultancy services to CIL; transactions comprise sales and dividend. A separate Coal India Limited (CIL) R&D relationship covers sales relating to R&D Board schemes.
- Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) — related party: Fellow CIL subsidiary under the same management; consultancy services sold to it. CMPDIL is Principal Implementing Agency for ECL for CBM development.
- Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) — related party: Fellow CIL subsidiary under the same management; consultancy services sold to it.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Diversify services and expand the client base beyond the Coal India ecosystem, with proactive visibility building through one-to-one meetings with target prospective clients, seminars/exhibitions, overseas exhibitions and social media outreach.
- Strategic shift towards diversification into the non-coal sector, using NMEDT funding for bauxite, base metal (copper, lead, zinc), magnetite and graphite exploration projects.
- Entry into critical minerals: acquired the Nawatala Devigarh REE exploration license block in Rajasthan in the first tranche of the Government of India exploration-license auction, and acted as transactional advisor for CIL in the acquisition of the Ontillu Chandragiri REE block in Andhra Pradesh.
- Collaboration with State Governments and State PSUs to increase nationwide visibility as a dependable solution provider.
- Enhance the pace of exploration by deploying 2D/3D seismic survey technologies, high-productivity drill machines, adoption of digital technology and latest exploration/mining software.
- Constant reskilling and upskilling of manpower, acquisition of latest equipment and software, and motivating teams to work with higher efficiency and responsibility.
- Continuous upgradation of laboratory capacity — including establishment of a Mineral Identification facility for non-coal and a fully operational ICP-MS laboratory for identification of Rare Earth Elements and trace metals.
- Build in-house report preparation capacity to reduce reliance on outsourcing, evidenced in Ground Water Modeling report preparation.
- Preserve the distinctiveness of the company for the interest of the coal sector as a whole even while diversifying.
- As a newly listed entity, remain committed to the highest standards of corporate governance, transparency, accountability and sustainable value creation for all stakeholders.
- The routed governance sections do not set out an explicit dividend, buyback or debt-reduction policy. Governance intent is framed instead as ensuring transparency, integrity, accountability, control and disclosure to achieve long-term corporate goals and enhance stakeholder value, with the Board receiving capital and revenue budgets, manpower budgets and periodic performance reviews, and approving the award of large contracts. The Audit Committee's mandate includes reviewing the statement of uses/application of funds raised through an issue (public issue, rights issue, preferential issue), monitoring the end use of funds raised through public offers including the funds raised through the Company's initial public offer, and scrutiny of inter-corporate loans and investments. The Company being a Government related entity is exempt from the general disclosure requirements in relation to related party transactions and outstanding balances with the controlling Governments and another entity under same Government, and reported NIL contracts or arrangements not at arm's length basis.
- Environmental services franchise: preparation, implementation and monitoring of Environment Management Plans through Regional Institutes and Headquarters for mining clients.
- Analysis of air, water and noise samples at in-house CPCB approved laboratories.
- Preparation of Mine closure plans and monitoring of mine closure.
- Environmental carrying capacity of mines and study of riverine ecosystem, including scientific sand replenishment studies for rivers in Bihar, 25 districts in Uttar Pradesh and various rivers in Rajasthan.
- Utilisation of remote sensing satellite data for land use monitoring across the entire set of CIL mines.
- Slope stability studies for overburden and highwall, supporting mine safety.
- Ventilation and gas surveys in mines, controlled blasting and performance evaluation of new explosives as safety-linked specialised services.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: CMPDIL's expansion in FY 2025-26 is capability- and platform-led rather than plant-led. The Company continued to operate from its Ranchi headquarter and seven Regional Institutes (Asansol, Dhanbad, Ranchi, Nagpur, Bilaspur, Singrauli and Bhubaneswar) while widening its consultancy footprint beyond the CIL ecosystem, onboarding more than 40 new clients and securing 142 outside-CIL consultancy jobs worth Rs 131.02 crores. In coal beneficiation it prepared feasibility reports for deshaling plants/washeries at Balaram-Hingula and Kulda-Garjanbahal in MCL and Bina-Kakri OCP in NCL, developed CIL's first model EPC bid document for washeries to standardise tendering across subsidiaries, prepared PFR and tender documents (RFQ-cum-RFP) for Dhori Washery (CCL) and New Moonidih Washery (BCCL), and provided services for setting up the Talabira Coal Washery at Talabira II & III OCP for NLCIL; a conceptual report and Notice Inviting Tender were developed with a pre-NIT meeting held on 21.03.2026. In unconventional energy, CMPDIL is Principal Implementing Agency for ECL, BCCL and SECL for CBM development: three CBM blocks (Jharia CBM Block-I, Raniganj CBM Block and Jharia CBM Block-II) are under consideration in CIL leasehold area, with Jharia CBM Block-I awarded to M/s Prabha Energy Limited on a revenue-sharing basis and currently in the exploration phase after completing 5 exploratory coreholes and 4 test wells, while Raniganj and Jharia CBM Block-II are proposed to be developed after selection of a CBM developer through tendering. An Underground Coal Gasification R&D pilot with ECL and Ergo Exergy Technology Inc. (Canada) completed Phase-I on 31st May 2025, with Phase-II covering pilot plant design, construction, commissioning, operation, shutdown and post-shutdown monitoring currently under implementation. An MoU was signed with the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons in May 2025 for data sharing and technology transfer on CBM and shale gas. On the research and digital side, a National Centre for Coal and Energy Research (NaCCER) has been established at CMPDIL, Ranchi; 13 research projects were completed and 40 remain ongoing; a 5G Centre of Excellence Use Case Test Lab with a lab-scale 5G Captive Non-Public Network was established with TCIL, with field R&D projects on 5G CNPN at the Amlohri Opencast Mine of NCL (with CDAC Thiruvananthapuram) and an underground mining application project with ITI Limited, Lucknow. CMPDIL developed and re-developed the Coal e-Auction platform under the Single Window Mode Agnostic Scheme 2022 with NIC as technology partner (over 8,000 registered bidders; 275 e-auctions conducted for more than 166 million tonnes of coal till March 2026) and is developing a portal for auction of coal under the modified SHAKTI Policy 2025 (Short Term).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Drilling volumes are expected to increase further in coming years, supported by sustained policy thrust and capacity augmentation initiatives.
- In June 2023 the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved continuation of Central Sector Schemes for exploration in coal and lignite during the 15th Finance Commission cycle up to 2025-26, underpinning the exploration workload.
- Faster proving of resources requires substantial expansion of CMPDIL's exploration role, met through departmental drilling capacity plus capacity of other agencies including MECL and outsourcing to private agencies.
- Diversification into non-coal and critical minerals (bauxite, base metals, magnetite, graphite, REE) opens a new demand pool beyond coal.
- Growth in Ground Water Modeling report preparation from 90 reports in the previous year to 136 in 2025-26 has effectively reduced reliance on outsourcing for GWM report preparation — an in-house cost/mix lever.
- Services extend beyond CIL to Ministry of Coal and MoP&NG for non-CIL blocks and coal-based non-conventional energy resources such as Coalbed Methane, Underground Coal Gasification and Shale Gas.
- Listing of equity shares on NSE and BSE during the year is presented as a step in the growth journey reflecting investor confidence in fundamentals and technical excellence.
- Accreditations (NABL/ISO/IEC 17025:2017, ICCP certification of petrographers) facilitate mutual acceptance of test results, supporting the laboratory services franchise.
- A pipeline of major project reports planned during 2025-26 for CIL: Recast PR of Magadh OC (51 Mty), CCL and Expansion PR of Lakhanpur Belpahar Lilari OCP (50 Mty), MCL.
- Other mega opencast projects planned for CIL include Jampali Expansion OC (20 Mty), SECL; Balbhadra North-West Expansion OC (20 Mty), MCL; Block F Reorganised OC (13 Mty), BCCL; Ongaon Potia OC (10 Mty), SECL and Recast PR of Durgapur OC (10 Mty), SECL.
- Two large underground projects planned during 2025-26: Inguri UG (4 Mty), NCL and Labji Pusla sector-1 UG (3 Mty), SECL.
- One opencast project report prepared for Rabodih OCP (2.5 Mty), a Non-CIL mine of M/s Twenty First Century Mining Pvt. Ltd.
- Two blocks for exploration of graphite granted by DGO, Orissa for implementation through NMEDT funding.
- One magnetite exploration project currently under progress.

deepdive.thesis: CMPDIL is a Mini Ratna (Cat-I) CPSE under the Ministry of Coal and an 85% subsidiary of Coal India Limited, positioned as India's leading total-solution mining consultancy covering exploration, mine planning & design and environmental services.

open.item: CMPDIL is in the process of procuring a rock cutting and polishing unit along with a Reflected Light Polarizing Research microscope to establish a Mineral Identification facility for non-coal minerals.

With NMEDT funding CMPDIL completed three bauxite exploration projects in Jharkhand and two base metal (copper, lead, zinc) projects, has one magnetite exploration project under progress, and has been granted two graphite exploration blocks by DGO, Orissa for implementation.

CMPDIL has established a dedicated 5G Centre of Excellence Use Case Test Lab with a lab-scale 5G Captive Non-Public Network in collaboration with TCIL, and is executing R&D projects on 5G CNPN for opencast mining at Amlohri Opencast Mine of NCL (with CDAC Thiruvananthapuram) and for underground mining applications with ITI Limited, Lucknow.
CMPDIL is developing a portal for conducting auction of coal under the modified SHAKTI Policy 2025 (Short Term), engaging NIC as its technology partner.

CMPDIL prepared PFR and tender documents (RFQ-cum-RFP) for Dhori Washery (CCL) and New Moonidih Washery (BCCL) and provided services for setting up the Talabira Coal Washery at Talabira II & III OCP for NLCIL.
Raniganj CBM Block and Jharia CBM Block-II are proposed to be developed after selection of a CBM developer through tendering.

Jharia CBM Block-I in the BCCL leasehold area has been awarded to M/s Prabha Energy Limited on a revenue-sharing basis and is currently in the exploration phase, with 5 exploratory coreholes and 4 test wells completed.

Phase-II of the Underground Coal Gasification R&D pilot with ECL and Ergo Exergy Technology Inc. (Canada) — covering pilot plant design, construction, commissioning, operation, shutdown and post-shutdown monitoring — is currently under implementation, Phase-I having completed on 31st May 2025.

Emphasis is being placed on diversifying R&D initiatives into environmental sustainability, energy management and digitization, carbon emission reduction, renewable energy, AI and IoT, waste-to-wealth creation and new exploration techniques.

A fully operational ICP-MS (Inductively Coupled Plasma-Mass Spectrometry) laboratory facility for qualitative and quantitative identification of Rare Earth Elements and trace metals is under process of being established.
The quantum of drilling is expected to increase further in the coming years, supported by sustained policy thrust and capacity augmentation initiatives.
CMPDIL secured the international assignment of ICVL for preparation of the DPR for the Tete East Project of ICVL Mozambique, a trackable overseas delivery commitment.

Several strategic MoUs, including one with NTPC Mining Limited (NML), are at various stages of finalization and are expected to further enhance the Company's service portfolio, technical capabilities and business prospects.
CMPDIL will continue diversifying its consultancy services beyond CIL, targeting public sector organizations, central and state government entities and private agencies.
Grow complete renewable-energy solutions including design, supply, installation, commissioning and O&M of grid-connected solar power systems
Advance CBM, CMM, underground and surface coal gasification and clean-coal technologies
Develop and implement customizable 5G use-case solutions for Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries via the 5G use-case test laboratory

risks.note: The Company's core role is in-house consultancy to CIL and its subsidiaries; the Board's Report frames FY 2025-26 progress explicitly as 'expanding its presence beyond the CIL ecosystem' and 'expanding its consultancy footprint beyond Coal India Limited', which implies the bulk of work continues to originate inside the parent group and that outside-CIL business (Rs 131.02 crore of orders in the year) is still a small complement.
risks.risk: Concentration on the Coal India Limited ecosystem

risks.note: The listed service lines — geological exploration and drilling for in-situ coal reserves, project reports for underground and opencast mines, coalfield master plans, coal beneficiation, utilisation and handling plants — are almost entirely coal-driven, so demand tracks coal exploration and mine-development activity rather than a diversified end-market.
risks.risk: Dependence on the coal sector and coal-linked capital cycle

risks.note: Growth beyond CIL depends on winning work from Central and State Government organizations, PSUs and private enterprises, and on MoUs (RITES, BSNL, and an NTPC Mining Limited MoU still at various stages of finalization). These are stated as expected to enhance the service portfolio and business prospects, i.e. benefits are not yet contracted.
risks.risk: Execution risk on the diversification strategy

risks.note: The REE Exploration License for the Navatala-Deogarh Block (Rajasthan) and the advisory-enabled Ontillu REE License mark a 'strategic entry into the critical mineral exploration domain'; a new domain carries geological, technical and commercial uncertainty relative to the established coal consultancy franchise.
risks.risk: Entry into new, unproven domains (critical minerals and REE)

risks.note: The Company operates as a Mini Ratna (Cat-I) government company whose services are substantially provided into government-directed programmes; the pace of exploration, project sanctioning and consultancy demand is therefore tied to government policy and budgetary decisions rather than to independent commercial demand.
risks.risk: Government / regulatory ownership and policy dependence

risks.note: The Report stresses the need for continuous efforts to enhance market outreach, deliver customized technical solutions and maintain high standards of quality and professionalism to sustain its 'competitive edge' — an acknowledgement that outside-CIL work is contested and must be won on merit against other consultancies.
risks.risk: Pricing and competitive pressure in an open consultancy market

risks.note: The service portfolio (planning, design, engineering, laboratory analysis, geomatics, ventilation and gas surveys, NDT, mine support design) is delivered by specialised technical manpower and laboratories across seven Regional Institutes and the Ranchi headquarter; capability, retention and equipment currency are the binding constraints on capacity.

Operations span a Ranchi headquarter plus seven Regional Institutes at Asansol, Dhanbad, Ranchi, Nagpur, Bilaspur, Singrauli and Bhubaneswar, alongside client assignments in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and an international assignment in Mozambique, which adds coordination and delivery-oversight complexity.

concerns_observed: Severe customer concentration: top-10 clients were ~95% of revenue and Coal India Limited group 66.0%-82.7% across periods; government entities/agencies were 96.0%-99.3%.

Governance gaps: no independent directors on the Board; operating under multiple SEBI exemptions from Listing-Regulations board and committee-composition norms until listing; director appointments controlled by the Government via the Ministry of Coal.
Related-party dependence: RPTs (largely CIL-group sales) were 74.2%-89.1% of revenue (net of levies); executive employees are seconded from Coal India Limited and secondment terms can change.
Government control: wholly owned by Coal India Limited / controlled by the Government of India, which can require actions serving national interest over minority-shareholder interests.
Structural demand risk from the energy transition and rising renewables reducing long-term coal-linked consultancy demand.

Audit/records issues: CAG supplementary audit, CARO remarks (title deed at Asansol not produced), an employee-fraud (EL encashment) instance, old outstanding debtors of Rs 99.23 crore (FY2025), and secretarial-records gaps for historical allotments.

red_flags: No independent directors and non-compliant board/committee composition, operating under time-limited SEBI exemptions.
Customer concentration with top-10 clients ~95% and CIL group up to 82.7% of revenue.
Instance of employee fraud (unauthorised earned-leave encashment) reported by the auditor for FY2025.
CARO observation that the title deed of land at CMPDI RI1 (Asansol) could not be produced for verification.
Old outstanding debtors of Rs 99.23 crore (FY2025) and a CIL-related balance management was unable to fully reconcile.
Secretarial-records gap: Form 2 for certain historical allotments unavailable or with typographical errors.
strengths_observed: Market-leading position: 61.0% share of the Indian mining consultancy market in Fiscal 2025 and preferred-consultant status with Coal India Limited.

Strong, profitable growth: revenue from operations grew from Rs 13,860.9 million (FY2023) to Rs 21,027.6 million (FY2025); PAT attributable to owners rose from Rs 2,966.6 million to Rs 6,669.1 million; RoNW 36.7% in FY2025.
Assured business pipeline from Maharatna parent Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries, with nomination-based / single-tender assignments providing revenue visibility.
Asset-light, high-return consultancy model with EBITDA of Rs 9,157.1 million in FY2025 and a nil-to-low debt profile.
Deep technical infrastructure: one of India's largest exploratory-drill fleets, seven regional institutes, eight laboratories, and recognized in-house R&D unit (443+ R&D projects).
Pure offer for sale by the promoter - no dilution to existing shareholders and no fresh-issue execution risk; WACA for Coal India Limited is only Rs 0.3 per share.
